I have farmed these 10 mu for 30 years. My father taught me the basics, and I finished middle school, so I can read labels and do sums. About eight years ago I went to a village training where the extension person talked about fertilizer balance — N, P, K, all that. I remember some of it, but mainly I do what has worked on my fields and what my neighbors do.

I split my land into two blocks. Six mu I do wheat-maize double cropping on — that is my main field, the good flat land by the well. The other 4.1 mu I plant potato in spring. 

For the winter wheat on the 6 mu, I plant an improved variety. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu, and this year I want to hit 500 kg. I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — the special blend from the dealer in town, about 16-25-0. Then at jointing I topdress with 15 kg of urea per mu. Altogether that is about 22 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate four times: winter irrigation once in November, then jointing, heading, and grain filling. The well water costs money for pumping, but four times is what everyone around here does and I am not going to risk it. I do rotary tillage before planting. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after emergence and fungicide once if the weather turns wet. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For the summer maize on that same 6 mu, I plant hybrid seed — Woyu or something similar from the seed shop. The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is only about seven days, so there is no time to plow. I use no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble. At planting I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then at the big trumpet stage I side-dress with urea. Total is about 20 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, at jointing and filling, because summer rain usually helps some. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide at planting and insecticide for corn borer in July. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the 4.1 mu of potato, I plant improved seed potato. Potatoes eat a lot of potassium, so I use 60 kg of high-K compound fertilizer per mu plus some extra potash. That works out to about 14 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 16 kg potassium per mu. I do rotary tillage to loosen the soil deep for the tubers. I irrigate four times because potatoes cannot stand drought, and I spray three times for late blight and aphids. I expect 2000 kg per mu.

My household has seven people. My son and daughter-in-law work in Shijiazhuang and send money home, so we have some cash. But fertilizer and diesel for the pump went up this year, so I am watching every yuan. Still, I will not cut back on fertilizer. Last year my neighbor Wang cut his wheat topdressing to save money and lost more than 100 kg per mu. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. I mostly do what I did last year. Change is risky, and I have a family to feed.
